column8: Wed 18 Nov: store only, Taiwan law (CASE_MAP A13); the statute's 31 August is Q49-003's, and the Constitution's 30 September is only the outer limit, so this adds nothing a part uses.

Wed 18 Nov: store only, Taiwan law (A13): a 2032 line left out of the cabinet's August 2031 draft cannot be added later, so a co-sponsor's figure has to reach the draft; background to rows 35-36, never in the report as law.
Wed 18 Nov: store only, Taiwan law (A13); reading a ministry's multi-year plan in its first budget book is Laura's own diligence, which 3d leaves out (Q92-035).

Wed 18 Nov: input to the 1 January reason (3c, 3d through row 35): agencies' 2032 estimates are drafted 1 May-6 Jun 2031, so a January figure is in time; schedule re-read at DGBAS today (114/5/1-114/6/6, policy by 114/3/28), one year's dates.

Wed 18 Nov: input to row 35 (3d, Table 3): ceilings set 25 Jul, cabinet 14 Aug, draft to the legislature 14-29 Aug, re-read at DGBAS today; asking a co-sponsor in late July is Laura's diligence, not report text.

Wed 18 Nov: store; verifies at source the 1-29 Aug window that Q49-007 held only from URL paths (re-read at DGBAS today: budget books of foundations over 50% government-endowed go to the legislature); use this row over Q49-007.

Wed 18 Nov: input to the 1 January reason (3c or 3d via row 35): 2032 ceilings are worked out from about Sep 2030 to Apr 2031, so a January 2031 figure lands while they are open; a summary table, not a statute.

Wed 18 Nov: store; the 15 April gate binds only plans of NT$1bn or more (row 9), so it is a reason for 1 January only if the residency sits inside a large public plan; GL000345 unreachable today, GL000455 pt 6 (DGBAS copy) says three months before the pre-review is settled, consistent.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; drop far above any residency facility in the case, since the case gives no facility cost and comparing to one is a cost estimate (A13); keep only that the gate catches cultural plans of NT$1bn or more.
Wed 18 Nov: store, input to row 11; FY2011's vote day unverified (debate 7-12 Jan 2011).

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5 and Table 3 row 7's note: updates Q49-026's on time in 0 of 11 to 0 of 17 (FY2010-26); fix FY2010-15 were 43-54 days late: FY2012 passed 13 Dec 2011, 13 days late, and FY2011's day is unverified, so say the January passages were 43-54 days late.

Wed 18 Nov: store (Q92-018 adds the same December pattern); replace about 18 Dec 2032 with December 2032 (IBTM's cash 20-22 Dec 2032, NUMBERS 8h; never 18 Dec); say on 3 of 4 precedents it may pass in Dec 2031, a habit, not a forecast.
Wed 18 Nov: Q49-025 already says the 2031 budget usually passes Dec 2030-Jan 2031, around the 2 Jan 2031 move; this adds only the local-election-year grouping (four cases, FY2011's day unverified).
Wed 18 Nov: store; promulgation lag 22-36 days checked (13 Dec-18 Jan 36, 15 Jan-6 Feb 22, 14 Aug-17 Sep 34); too fine a date for Table 3, which has no room for a new row.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; whether the Ministry's residency money sits in a special fund was not checked, so it serves no part yet.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5 wording guard: 257 days after its deadline, and if a second figure helps 226 days into the year it was for; CNA re-read today (passed 14 Aug 2026, the latest ever, the Speaker's 266 with no base); the press's 351 never as days late.
Wed 18 Nov: store; referral to committees as an early warning is one year's case, and Table 3 has no room for a new row (A34 kept).
Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5 beside Q49-012: new programmes and new local grants, the kind a residency co-sponsor gives, are what a late budget holds back; sizes the rule in its worst year (NT$101.7bn new).
Wed 18 Nov: store only; live news, outcome unknown; 5 Jan 2027 is 36 days after 30 Nov 2026 (checked).
Wed 18 Nov: store only; a supplementary budget cannot be planned on and Art. 79 was not read.
Wed 18 Nov: store, input to row 26; Kaohsiung's 6 Feb 2026 third reading is 68 days after 30 Nov (checked); one city.
Wed 18 Nov: store, input to row 26; the city's internal estimate deadline is unconfirmed (Gaps), so a mid-2031 cut-off is inference.
Wed 18 Nov: store, input to row 26: in a local-election year a city votes early or leaves the budget to the new council; two cities, opposite habits.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; posting dates, not vote dates, and Table 3 has no room for a city row.
Wed 18 Nov: store, input to row 26; one year of Taipei's draft date.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d through row 35: a city co-sponsor can carry a January 2031 figure into its 2032 draft, while its 2033 money may be voted after Laura pays in December 2032, consistent with public running money following that payment; Keel's pattern on three cities.
Wed 18 Nov: store; NCAF's fund is 99.93% government money (7,075,130,762 of 7,080,000,000, checked), so it budgets on the state's calendar; closes Q49-007's open endowment share.
Wed 18 Nov: input to rows 30 and 35 (3c, Table 3): NCAF's 2032 budget is settled about April-August 2031, after a 1 January 2031 figure; posting dates from file folders.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; statute (A13), and a quarterly board's lag serves no part; Q92-014 has the terms.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5 and 3c's 1 January reason, once fixed: the top is owned at the 1 Jan 2031 move, so a 2031 fall cannot lower it (NUMBERS 8p: after the move only her flexibility falls), while NCAF's 2032 budget, set mid-2031 on a fund about 57% in shares, can fall; say share markets, not the same markets as VT (the book names no market); quote and mix re-read today.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d: many listed companies set next year's budget in November-December, so a January 2031 figure gives a company co-sponsor most of a year; seven boards, a search sample, never all (Q50: most keep no fixed sponsorship budget).
Wed 18 Nov: 3d's evidence for the company half: Chang Wah's board passed its 2026 budget and a separate 2026 donation budget on 18 Dec 2025, re-read at source today; one firm.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d and Table 3, a calendar reason for the 1 January 2031 move (DGBAS inputs re-read today); fix after about June 2031 public money reaches only 2033: the row's own NCAF January 2032 and village November 2031 rounds are 2032 money, and city drafts run to 30 Sep, so say most public 2032 drafts close by mid-2031.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c (beside 8r; 3b is the contribution, not the move) and 3d: a second reason for 1 January, never the only one; strike not a money choice and calendars, not the markets: 8r keeps January for the case's 2031 meetings and because a later move lowers the top in 12.0% (April) or 15.7% (July) of house paths; a July figure misses every public draft is unverified (city drafts to 30 Sep, internal deadlines unknown); the April gate binds only NT$1bn plans.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d's timing line in Laura's voice, the year named (in January 2031, in time for your 2032 budget), and the conceit's front edge: no figure before the move (IPS l.15 read); fix January-March 2031 is the whole window: ministries' estimates run to 6 Jun and city drafts to Jul-Sep, so say a January 2031 figure reaches every kind of co-sponsor's 2032 budget.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 3 row 7's note beside Q49-026, only if room (one page, no new row, A34 kept): the dated public watch for 2032 money (Aug draft, Oct referral, Dec passage on 3 of 4 precedents, Jan promulgation); a late or frozen budget never changes the plan.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5: a late budget delays new money and old programmes run on (row 18, Q49-012); but never define IPS l.15's falling short or say her flexibility does not answer a late payer (Q92-036 reads a delay as that case; evaluate, never add a rule), and drop a few weeks late (FY2026 was 257 days after its deadline).
